title: One Remote, Two Kids, Nine Boards: Tic-Tac-Toe on the TV | vitalii.no
description:
The family kiosk had quiz walls and lesson cards, but nothing the kids could play together. Any two-player game on one TV with one remote runs into the same wall: how do you tell which of two kids pressed which button, and how do you explain the rules to a child who can't read a full rulebook yet.

I added Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe as a new kiosk game, reachable through a game button on the TV page. Each player identifies with their own PIN before taking a turn - parents get a game-only PIN so they can join in too - X and O are assigned at random, and a Cloudflare Worker keeps the running score table between matches. A second commit added a rules button that opens a child-level explanation of the rules mid-game, without losing the current board.

Two kids can now sit on one sofa, share one remote, and play a full nine-board match identified only by their PINs, with the score kept automatically match over match.
